attempted_claim: Let K be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and R=K[x,y,z]. Let A=R/Ann(F) be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein K-algebra of codimension 3 with h-vector (1,3,6,10,10,6,3,1) (socle degree 7, Sperner number 10, two consecutive peaks). Does A necessarily have the weak Lefschetz property, i.e. for a general linear form l in A_1 is the multiplication map A_3 -> A_4 an isomorphism?
decisive_failure: The investigation reduced the target to identical vanishing of the third Hessian of a compressed ternary septic and probed it with exact symbolic block factorizations plus corrected global numerical optimization, but it could not prove universal nonvanishing (which needs a new Gordan-Noether-type theorem) nor exhibit an exact compressed counterexample; all vanishing loci found carry a constant kernel forcing non-compressedness. Verdict: target blocked with no auditable claim.
